The Invisible Kingpin: The Drug Lord No One Knew https://youtu.be/WL1kt3c6w1s

Follow me on Instagram! https://www.instagram.com/_pablitos_way/

6 - Bail Me Out Daddy
When police found Marcus Jordan- son of his Royal Air-ness, Michael Jordan- his $300,000 Lamborghini was stuck on train tracks, half-buried in rocks. Instead of taking the situation seriously, he argued with officers, insisted they could push the car off the tracks, and—most embarrassingly—dropped the classic “Do you know who my dad is?” line. At 34 years old.

5 - No Codes
When officers stopped a man known only as AJ near Key West for multiple boat code violations, he seemed irritated but cooperative. First, they asked for his ID—no problem. But when his girlfriend- obviously seizing an opportunity- started demanding his phone’s passcode, and he did what anyone with nothing to hide would do—he jumped overboard and made a break for it.

4 - The Contortionist
Some people fold under pressure. Others fold themselves into a clothes dryer. David Jerome Jackson, 31, who was a wanted man, thought he could spin his way out of trouble by cramming himself into a tiny clothes dryer. But, unfortunately for Jackson, these deputies didn’t skip laundry day.

3 - Amish Party
An Ohio deputy found himself in an unusual pursuit when he encountered Amish man Nathan Miller slumped over in a moving horse and buggy. The incident occurred in the early hours of the morning in Orwell, Ohio, when Ashtabula Sheriff’s Deputy Mike Talbert spotted Miller's buggy drifting all over the road, which was probably super weird to see.

2 - Personal Tags
A renowned British surgeon, Simon Bramhall, wound up at the center of controversy after it was discovered that he was burning his initials into the livers of two patients during transplant surgeries. The incidents occurred at Birmingham’s Queen Elizabeth Hospital in the UK, where Bramhall used an argon beam—normally employed to stop bleeding and mark areas for surgical precision—to inscribe "SB" on the transplanted organs.

1 - The Missing Stash
Florida woman Lily Rinker learned the hard way that some problems are better left unsolved—especially when you have active warrants. Lily dialed 911 from a Best Western hotel at 2 in the morning to report that some guy named Carlos had taken a small amount of her stash and left. Unsure of what to do, she turned to emergency services—because, apparently, for Rinker, that was an emergency.

The Invisible Kingpin: The Drug Lord No One Knew https://youtu.be/WL1kt3c6w1s

Follow me on Instagram! https://www.instagram.com/_pablitos_way/

6 - Planting Charges
In March of 2018, a guy named Jason Serrano was still recovering from a prior injury and barely able to stand upright when he became the target of NYPD officers Kyle Erickson and Elmer Pastran. The officers had pulled over Serrano and his friend for an alleged broken taillight—something they couldn’t have seen from their original position, and what followed was a cascade of events so ridiculous that it almost sounds fake. Like a case of cops gone wrong. 

5 - Transparent Fraud
Here’s a delightful tale of true crime served with a side of Cancun margaritas. Brandon Anderson, an anti-police activist and founder of Raheem Al, which was a chatbot that helps the public monitor police interactions, allegedly decided that the best way to fight for police transparency was by being as opaque as possible with $75,000 in donations. We know, you’d never expect an activist to be shady, right?

4 - Overreacting Dad or Overreacting Bad Cops?
Imagine this: you call 911 because your child has been taken by her mother, who’s struggling with substance misuse. You’re panicked, desperate, and expecting the police to step in and help- something the police are supposed to do. Instead, Darnay Cockrell found himself starring in a real-life demonstration of how to turn a crisis into a fiasco, courtesy of the Mesa Police Department.

3 - The Aggressive Arrest 
It took three years for Officer Gonzalo Zendejas to face a single charge of misconduct under the color of authority after being caught on video punting a 17-year-old suspected shoplifter in the face. The incident went down back in June of 2021 at a Glendale, California, sporting goods store, and didn't just involve Zendejas—it featured a whole group of plainclothes and uniformed officers- AKA grown ass men- piling on the teen like some kind of weird team-building exercise.

2 - Hoop Dreams
Scammers have devised a clever way to con well-meaning New Yorkers, and unfortunately, it’s working all too well. Over $76,000 has been stolen in a growing city-wide scam involving fake basketball team donations. The NYPD has identified at least 39 cases in Manhattan and Brooklyn in 2024, and the numbers are climbing.

1 - Animal Rescue Ponzi
Remember Johanna Michely Garcia, the self-proclaimed "Mother Theresa" of South Florida who turned out to be more of a financial grim reaper? Garcia had run a nearly $200 million Ponzi scheme disguised as an investment company, MJ Capital Funding. Well, she’s back in the spotlight—this time with a shiny new 20-year prison sentence. So, the ringleader of an infamous $200 million Ponzi scheme just got handed the maximum punishment. Let’s unpack this mess.
